title: Sysmon or Built-In Windows Auditing: How Much Endpoint Logging Do You Need?
excerpt: Windows has native security auditing; Sysmon, from Microsoft Sysinternals, adds much richer event data. This comparison explains what each gives a SOC and when the extra detail is worth it.
verdict: Sysmon gives far more detail, such as process hashes, network connections and parent-child process chains, and pays off when a SIEM is analysing the data. Built-in auditing is a reasonable starting point, but on its own it is rarely enough for a real investigation. Most mature environments run both.
